title: Germany's New Photonic XPU Just Made Nvidia & AMD GPUs Look Like Paper Weights!
excerpt:
Akhetonics is building one of the most ambitious chips in the world: a true all-optical processor that uses light instead of electrons to compute. As AI data centers consume more power than ever, photonic computing could become the next major breakthrough in chip technology. This video explores how Akhetonics, a German startup based in Munich and Berlin, is developing its XPU, a cross-domain photonic processor designed to combine digital, analog, and quantum photonics on one platform. We break down why photons could solve the heat and energy problems holding back traditional silicon chips, how wavelength multiplexing can unlock massive bandwidth, and why this technology could change the future of AI hardware.

From their world-first general-purpose all-optical 2-bit CPU demo to their plan for a full prototype by 2026, Akhetonics is trying to challenge the limits of Moore’s Law and build a new future for European chip innovation. Could light-based chips become the next big threat to Nvidia, GPUs, and traditional semiconductor computing?
